answer: Attackers run many sybils from one backend, so their mistakes copy each other. Give every identity a different noisy sample of the same public event — one counts a raven at dawn, another reads an ocean buoy, a third tests umber sediment — then require a committed report before the full record opens. Honest observers converge on the truth yet differ in noise; farm copies share identical gaps and errors, so correlated-error clusters lose standing while independent reporters keep it.
